The Alpha-3 Nimbus-class Interceptor, better known as the V-Wing, is a fast, agile starfighter with exceptional survivability for its class. Equipped with rapidly recharging shields and an onboard astromech, it can outlast most light interceptors in prolonged dogfights. Its light repeating laser cannons are highly effective against fragile targets, allowing it to quickly eliminate droid starfighters and other lightly armored craft. However, the lack of missiles or heavier weapons limits its effectiveness against shielded or durable opponents. While outdated by the Galactic Civil War, the V-Wing remains a capable interceptor, able to reliably contest modern light fighters when used in its intended role.

The Eta-2 Actis-class Interceptor was developed by Kuat Systems Engineering as an advanced light interceptor, intended to replace the older Delta-7. Like its predecessor, it was often incorrectly referred to as the “Jedi Starfighter” due to its widespread use by Jedi Knights during the Clone Wars. In reality, the Eta-2 was mass-produced alongside other Republic starfighters and saw extensive frontline service throughout the war. Outfitted with folding S-foils and an astromech droid for onboard repairs, it was armed with light laser cannons and ion cannons, giving it a rare edge against shielded targets.

Extremely fast and maneuverable, the Eta-2 is difficult to hit, partially offsetting its complete lack of shields. Its ion weaponry makes it especially effective when supporting other fighters, allowing it to disable enemy craft for follow-up attacks. However, its fragility makes it unforgiving in direct engagements, requiring careful positioning and constant movement to survive.

HP: 36, Armor: Medium, Max Speed: 3.5, Agility: 1.9 Active Abilities: Hunt, Overcharge Lasers Passive Abilities: None 6 units per squadron.

By the time the Clone Wars erupted in 22 BBY, Slayn & Korpil’s V-19 Torrent was already considered obsolete and was being phased out of service. Nevertheless, the Republic Navy possessed millions of these mass-produced fighters and, out of logistical necessity, deployed them against the Confederacy. Armed with a concussion missile launcher and a pair of light laser cannons, and offering slightly above-average handling, the V-19 was a broadly capable but unremarkable starfighter.

Lacking both shields and a hyperdrive, it was entirely dependent on carrier support and vulnerable in prolonged engagements. Despite these limitations, the V-19 proved effective against the swarms of lightly armored droid starfighters fielded by the Confederacy, where its numbers and balanced performance allowed it to hold its own. Though considered outdated, it remained in service throughout the war, only being fully replaced following the rise of the Galactic Empire.

The Incom-built Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 (ARC-170) is a heavy multi-role starfighter introduced late in the Clone Wars, and an early Incom design that influenced the later X-wing. Equipped with folding S-foils, the ARC-170 can enter an attack position for combat or close its wings to increase engine output for pursuit or disengagement. Heavily armed and durable, it excels in fire-support roles, with powerful forward heavy laser cannons capable of damaging gunships and lightly armored starships. An onboard astromech enables in-flight repairs, while dual rear turrets provide defensive coverage against pursuing fighters.

Although less maneuverable than dedicated interceptors, the ARC-170 is difficult to bring down and can hold its own in dogfights. It performs best when engaging larger targets or supporting bomber formations, where its heavy firepower can be brought to bear. Escort fighters are recommended to screen nimble enemy craft that the ARC-170 may struggle to track reliably.

Prioritizing speed and agility above all else, the elegant N-1 Starfighter is a high-performance light interceptor used exclusively by the Royal Naboo forces. Extremely small and difficult to hit, it combines rapid maneuverability with quickly recharging shields and an onboard astromech for limited in-flight repairs. These traits allow the N-1 to evade incoming fire and outmaneuver slower opponents in sustained dogfights.

However, the N-1 is lightly armed, carrying only twin repeating laser cannons and a homing torpedo launcher. While effective against lightly armored targets, it struggles to damage shielded or heavily armored craft, and can be overwhelmed by more heavily armed interceptors capable of breaching its defenses. It performs best when engaging nimble fighters where its speed and precision can be fully exploited.

Required Planets (Empire, Neutral, Rebel, Republic, Underworld): Naboo

Developed alongside the N-1, the N-1B Starbomber is a larger, three-seat strike variant that retains the same emphasis on speed and agility. Equipped with four engines and only slightly less maneuverable than its interceptor counterpart, the N-1B is unusually nimble for a bomber. Strong shielding, a small profile, and an onboard astromech allow it to evade incoming fire and survive attack runs that would overwhelm heavier strike craft.

The N-1B carries a payload of proton torpedoes for engaging starships and hardened targets, supported by twin light laser cannons and a rear-mounted twin laser turret for defense against pursuing fighters. While lightly armed for dogfighting and less durable than dedicated bombers, its speed and precision make it highly effective in hit-and-run strikes, slipping past defenses to deliver torpedoes before disengaging.

The Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor was a Republic air superiority fighter produced by Kuat Systems Engineering shortly before the Clone Wars. Commonly associated with the Jedi Order, it was designed for extreme speed and maneuverability, offering rapid acceleration and excellent handling in combat. While it features respectable shielding for its size, most models lacked a built-in hyperdrive, relying instead on carrier deployment or hyperspace rings, though later variants addressed this limitation.

Armed with only a pair of light laser cannons, the Delta-7 struggles against heavily armored or shielded targets. It excels in dogfights against lightly armored craft, where its speed and agility allow it to outmaneuver opponents and control engagements. Against stronger enemies, it is best used to harass and delay until heavier support can be brought to bear.

Setting the standard for the later and more famous BTL-A4, Koensayr Manufacturing’s BTL-B Y-Wing served the Republic with distinction during the Clone Wars. Durable, reliable, and versatile, it features strong shielding, a heavily armored chassis, and an astromech for onboard repairs. A light laser turret provides all-around defensive coverage, while forward-mounted medium lasers, ion torpedoes, and proton torpedoes allow it to deliver significant damage against capital ships.

However, the BTL-B is slow and highly unresponsive, making it vulnerable to interception. Without proper escort, it can be quickly overwhelmed and destroyed by enemy fighters, and performs best when supported by allied starfighters to ensure its payload reaches the target.

The Y-Wing is the workhorse of the Rebel fleet. It's not quick or flashy, but it gets the job done. The armor on this ship is extensive, and the shields will protect you from just about anything, which is good, because you won't be going anywhere fast. The Y-Wing is used mainly as a bomber because it can carry a heavy payload of missiles, torpedoes, and bombs. As with most Rebel starfighters, the Y-Wing carries an onboard astromech droid for in-flight repairs. Armed with a medium dual laser cannon, concussion missiles, and an ion cannon turret, it can engage enemy starfighters and gunships, though its slow speed and poor maneuverability limit its effectiveness in dogfights.

The Z-95 CVB (Clone Variant Bomber) was a Republic-developed strike fighter conversion of the Z-95 CVI fielded during the Clone Wars to provide a fast, inexpensive ordnance delivery platform. Retaining the interceptor-derived airframe, the CVB emphasized speed and maneuverability over protection, allowing it to reach targets more quickly than conventional bombers but leaving it significantly more vulnerable once committed to an attack run.

Designed to strike capital ships and orbital installations with light proton torpedoes and armor-piercing missiles, the CVB reflected the Republic’s willingness to accept higher attrition in exchange for aggressive, high-tempo assault capability. While effective in skilled hands, its limited survivability meant that many missions carried extreme risk for its clone pilots, a tradeoff that Republic planners ultimately deemed acceptable given the craft’s low cost and rapid production.

Developed from the standard Z-95 Headhunter, the Z-95 “Hullcracker” is a strike-focused variant that leverages the fighter’s modular ordnance launcher to replace concussion missiles with proton torpedoes. This simple modification allows the Hullcracker to function as a light, low-cost bomber capable of threatening capital ships and orbital installations. Poorly armored and lightly defended, it is undeniably crude by modern military standards, but its affordability and ease of maintenance have made it a favorite among pirates, criminal syndicates, and irregular forces. When deployed in numbers, the Hullcracker can overwhelm point defenses and deliver surprisingly devastating damage, ensuring it remains a threat that cannot be safely ignored.

The Z-95 CVI (Clone Variant Interceptor) was the original production model of the Z-95 line, developed by Incom for the Republic Navy during the Clone Wars as a proposed new standard for Republic starfighters. Unlike earlier designs such as the Eta-2 or V-19 Torrent, the CVI was built from the outset with deflector shields and an integrated hyperdrive, reflecting a doctrinal shift toward independent, long-range starfighter operations without reliance on docking rings or constant carrier support.

Designed specifically around clone pilot physiology and training, the Z-95 CVI featured extremely aggressive flight characteristics, offering exceptional acceleration and maneuverability that were difficult for non-clone pilots to fully exploit, but came at the cost of a lighter and less durable airframe. While later eclipsed by more refined successors, the CVI proved effective in service and laid the foundation for the Headhunter lineage that followed.

Developed by Incom as a simplified successor to the Clone Wars–era Z-95 CVI, the Z-95 Headhunter was designed to be inexpensive, rugged, and easy to mass-produce. Many of the complex and maintenance-heavy systems of its predecessor were deliberately stripped away, resulting in a straightforward general-purpose starfighter well suited to militias, planetary defense forces, and pirates. While clearly outclassed by modern starfighters, the Z-95 remains serviceable thanks to its reliability, wide availability, and flexible design. Of particular note is its modular ordnance launcher system, allowing the Headhunter to carry either missiles or torpedoes depending on mission requirements. Long past its prime, the Z-95 endures not through superiority, but through affordability, familiarity, and adaptability.

The Z-95 CVMR (Clone Variant Multi-Role) was an advanced evolution of the original Z-95 CVI, redesigned from the ground up with a new fuselage, engines, wings, and upgraded systems. Featuring stronger shields, improved engine performance, enhanced maneuverability, extended-range laser cannons, and double the ordnance capacity, the CVMR was intended to bridge the gap between interceptor and strike bomber roles. Capable of excelling in both dogfighting and precision strike missions, it was reserved for the most highly trained clone pilots. These improvements came at a significant cost, however, making the CVMR far more expensive to produce and limiting its deployment despite its exceptional performance.

The Rapid-32 Assault Interceptor, or R-32, is a space superiority starfighter developed by Incom Corporation in the final months of the Clone Wars. Designed as a hyperspace-capable interceptor, it combines strong speed and maneuverability with a versatile weapons suite. Light and medium laser cannons provide reliable dogfighting performance, while concussion missiles and powerful ion-pulse missiles allow the R-32 to disable shielded targets and deliver a decisive opening strike.

Ion-pulse missiles are particularly effective against high-value or heavily shielded opponents, briefly crippling defenses and leaving targets vulnerable to follow-up attacks. While not intended for prolonged engagements against large fighter swarms, the R-32 excels at engaging elite craft and priority targets, making it a capable and dangerous interceptor in Republic service.

The J-45 “Heavy Sabre” is a heavily armed strike variant of the standard J-45, optimized for engaging warships and hardened targets. High-velocity heavy laser cannons allow it to engage gunships and corvettes at long range with exceptional accuracy, while its ordnance pods carry a mix of plasma torpedoes and advanced proton torpedoes capable of stripping shields or bypassing them to damage critical subsystems on larger capital ships. This loadout gives the Heavy Sabre significant anti-ship striking power in a compact platform.

However, these heavier weapons come at the cost of anti-starfighter performance. Slower firing cannons and reduced agility leave the Heavy Sabre at a disadvantage in dogfights, making it vulnerable to interceptors. Like the standard model, it relies on its SLAM drive for attack runs and disengagement, and performs best when escorted by friendly fighters.

The J-45 “Sabre” is an advanced twin-seat multirole fighter developed by Rothana Heavy Engineering and Koensayr Manufacturing. It features underslung missile pods loaded with both armor-piercing and high-explosive warheads, allowing it to engage a wide range of targets. Four rapid-firing medium repeating laser cannons provide strong anti-starfighter capability, making the Sabre effective against both fighters and larger vessels.

Despite its versatility, the Sabre is relatively slow with a wide turning radius, leaving it vulnerable to more agile interceptors. An onboard astromech enables in-flight repairs, while a Sub Light Accelerator Motor (SLAM drive) allows it to rapidly reposition, disengage, or execute hit-and-run attacks.

Developed by Kuat Systems Engineering for the Republic, the R-22 “Spearhead” was designed to replace the V-19, Delta-7, and Eta-2 as part of a broader shift toward independent starfighter doctrine. Unlike its predecessors, the R-22 combined shielding, extreme maneuverability, and a compact profile with an integrated hyperdrive, eliminating the need for docking rings and allowing it to operate independently across multiple theaters. This made the Spearhead well suited to the Republic’s growing reliance on fast-deploying fleets and deep-space operations.

As the Clone Wars drew to a close, the program was abandoned, with the Imperial Navy rejecting it in favor of the cheaper TIE line built around mass production and carrier reliance. Diverted to civilian and black market sales, the R-22 found new life among rebel cells, criminal syndicates, and independent factions. With exceptional speed, agility, respectable shielding, and repeating laser cannons capable of extremely high rates of fire, it proved more than a match for contemporary starfighters, and its combat record would later influence Kuat’s next generation of interceptors, culminating in the RZ-1 A-Wing.

The GAT-12 Skipray Blastboat is a rugged gunboat-bomber hybrid developed by Republic Sienar Systems prior to the Clone Wars. Large, heavily armored, and equipped with strong shields, a missile jamming suite, and an astromech for in-flight repairs, it is designed to engage targets well above its weight class. A medium laser turret provides defensive coverage, while long-range ion cannons and a heavy payload of proton torpedoes make the Skipray especially effective against gunships and capital ships.

However, the Skipray’s size and limited speed make it an easy target for interceptors. Though highly capable, its complexity and cost prevented widespread adoption, and it was ultimately overshadowed by cheaper dedicated strike craft. Many surplus Skiprays later found service with pirates and militia forces, where their durability and firepower made them formidable bomber platforms.

The massive PT-1 Gunship is a strange and unconventional design originally commissioned by the Theed Palace Space Vessel Engineering Corps of Naboo. Built as a fast anti-starfighter platform, the PT-1 is essentially two enormously powerful engines attached to a large dual crew module and a broad, one-piece armored wing that forms most of the craft’s structure. Armed with heavy laser cannons and high-explosive missiles, it was intended to obliterate enemy squadrons in a single devastating volley before retreating at extreme speed.

For in-atmosphere operations, few gunships are as effective as Rothana Heavy Engineering’s LAAT/i (Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry), but in space it is far less exceptional. Poorly shielded and a large, slow target, it remains heavily armed with armor-piercing missile launchers, medium laser turrets, and composite beam cannons. These beam weapons are particularly effective against starfighters, allowing the LAAT to quickly eliminate light craft. Despite its firepower, its lack of durability and speed leaves it vulnerable in space combat, where it performs as only an average gunship.

A mixed group of CEC YT-series light freighters, commonly used across the galaxy by traders, smugglers, and pirates due to their modular and easily modified design. While these examples lack the extensive custom upgrades seen on famous vessels like the Millennium Falcon or Outrider, they retain the durability and versatility that made the platform so popular.

Equipped with turreted laser cannons offering wide firing coverage, these freighters can function as makeshift gunships. Heavy armor and shielding allow them to absorb punishment, while their respectable agility for ships of their size lets them support starfighters and lay down sustained fire during dogfights.

Designed for the Republic during the mid-stages of the Clone Wars, the XB-17 Heavy Tactical Bomber was one of the largest starcraft Incom ever produced. Nicknamed the “Big Dumb Bomber,” it sacrificed speed and agility in favor of a massively reinforced hull and thick armor plating, allowing it to absorb punishment while delivering devastating strikes. Armed with a huge payload of proton torpedoes, the XB-17 excelled at crippling CIS warships and orbital targets, while its medium laser turrets provided basic protection against droid fighters. By the time of the Galactic Civil War it was already obsolete and extremely vulnerable to modern interceptors, yet it continued to see limited service with the Rebel Alliance, which pressed it into combat out of necessity rather than choice.

Designed and built by Corellian Engineering Corporation prior to the Clone Wars, the Gozanti-class is a rugged and versatile workhorse long used by both the Republic and the Imperial Navy. Primarily an armed transport, the Gozanti can carry starfighters or light vehicles directly into combat using quick-release clamps mounted beneath its hull, allowing it to rapidly deploy and recover assets in contested space.

Armed with forward-firing proton torpedo launchers and twin heavy laser turrets providing near-total coverage, the Gozanti is capable of striking hardened targets or defending itself against enemy bombers. Deployable starfighter repair droids and onboard astromech systems allow it to support nearby fighters while maintaining its own combat readiness. Though slow and cumbersome, with a large and easily targeted profile, the Gozanti remains a valuable fleet support vessel where flexibility and endurance matter more than speed.

Required Planets (Republic, Underworld): Corellia, Ringo_Vinda, Rendili, Rothana, Allanteen

The C70 Charger-class corvette was a combat refit of the Consular-class civilian diplomatic vessel, developed in the early days of the Clone Wars when the Republic possessed few purpose-built warships. Equipped with light armor plating, five heavy laser turrets, an Intermediate Range Anti-Starfighter (IRAS) missile launcher, and an advanced targeting computer, the C70 excels as an escort and reconnaissance platform. Its armament is well suited for anti-starfighter operations and the interception of enemy gunships, while powerful engines and excellent maneuverability allow it to rapidly pursue fleeing targets or disengage from unfavorable engagements.

The Defense Penetrator-20 Gunboat, developed by Corellian Engineering Corporation, was designed to supplement the CR90 by taking on a more aggressive combat role. Rather than focusing on fighter screening, the DP-20 emphasizes raw offensive capability with rapid-fire light turbolasers, dual medium laser cannons, and armor-piercing missile launchers. Small, fast, and highly maneuverable, it excels in hit-and-run tactics, darting in to unleash a crippling barrage before retreating beyond enemy firing arcs. However, the DP-20 relies almost entirely on speed for survival, as its armor and shields are extremely weak. When paired with bomber strikes, it becomes a deadly force multiplier capable of tearing holes in enemy capital ships far beyond what its modest size would suggest.

The Corellian Engineering Corporation CR90-class Corvette, often referred to as the blockade runner, is renowned for being among the fastest corvettes ever produced. With its four rapid-fire medium laser cannons and two light turbolaser turrets linked to an advanced fire-control system, the CR90 is an excellent fighter screener and the corvette of choice for Rebel commanders looking to shield their fleets from waves of Imperial TIEs. Although the CR90 is unfit for ship-to-ship combat, it comes equipped with missile-jamming countermeasures and the ability to channel extra reactor power to the engines for a quick escape.

The XX-777 Crusader-class Droid Platform, commonly known as the Droid Corvette, is a fully automated warship developed through a joint venture between Corellian Engineering and Loronar. Despite its Core World origins, the XX-777 saw widespread use within the Confederate Navy and later among Separatist holdout forces, aided by extensive corporate espionage networks.

Cheap, lightly armored, and barely shielded, the “triple seven” is built for simple, aggressive tactics, with all weapons mounted forward for direct assault runs and swarming attacks. It is armed with light turbolasers, ion cannons, and concussion missiles, allowing it to provide long-range ion fire support while also threatening corvettes and gunships. Highly maneuverable and equipped with a missile jamming system, the XX-777 relies on numbers rather than durability to survive.

SP: 1500 (20/s) HP: 2000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 5, Agility: 0.75 Sensor Range: 2750m, Max Engagement Range: 3250m Active Abilities: Power To Engines Passive Abilities: None

Weapons: x4 Light Turbolaser, x4 Heavy Flak Laser Cannon, x12 Medium Repeating Laser Cannon

The Corellian Engineering Corporation’s C-9 “Sentinel”-class is a dedicated anti-starfighter corvette designed to protect larger warships from hostile strikecraft. Heavily armed for its size, it mounts twelve medium repeating laser cannons and four heavy flak laser batteries, making it exceptionally lethal against fighters and bombers.

For defense against larger vessels, the Sentinel carries only a minimal armament of four light turbolasers, leaving it unsuited for frontline engagements. Instead, it relies on its powerful engines, tight turning capability, and rapid acceleration to evade threats it cannot directly confront. In its intended role, the C-9 excels as a fast-moving escort, screening capital ships and tearing apart incoming strikecraft before they can deliver their payloads.

Required Planets: Ringo_Vinda, Rendili, Rothana, Allanteen, Corellia

Jak Kannadee is something of an enigma. He was found at the Polis Massa medical center after suffering severe head trauma consistent with a slugthrower but is either unwilling or unable to provide details of how he suffered it. His larger-than-life personality, hard to place accent and lack of any official documentation all drew concerned questions when Kannadee subsequently enlisted in the Republic Navy. However, no one can deny his effectiveness. Within 6 months, Jak Kannadee was commanding his own Consular-class, requesting the designation CR-109.

Developed by Kuat Drive Yards shortly before the Clone Wars, the Arquitens-class was quickly integrated into the Republic Navy and saw widespread deployment across nearly every major theater. Originally intended for patrol, picket, and escort duties, the Arquitens proved highly adaptable in frontline engagements. Armed with light turbolasers, heavy laser cannons, and anti-strikecraft concussion (ASC) missiles, it is well equipped for both ship-to-ship combat and fighter screening.

What sets it apart from other corvettes of the era is its impressive speed and agility, allowing it to chase down fleeing targets and reposition quickly in battle. With a balanced mix of firepower, mobility, and moderate durability, the Arquitens serves as a flexible all-rounder capable of fulfilling many roles, though exceptional in none.

A decorated veteran of the Battle of Naboo, Quarsh Panaka rose to prominence as head of the Naboo Royal Security Forces. Known for his unyielding loyalty and sharp tactical instincts, Panaka led the defense of Theed alongside Queen Padmé Amidala, engaging in brutal close-quarters combat to reclaim the capital from Trade Federation occupation.

With the onset of the Clone Wars, Panaka assumed command of Naboo’s planetary defense forces and was given an Arquitens-class Light Cruiser, which he personally modified and christened The Contrarian. Built for tactical flexibility, The Contrarian features an enhanced shield generator, reinforced armor plating, and a complement of astromech droids for on-the-fly hull repairs. Its firepower is augmented by an additional dual light turbolaser turret, heavy flak laser cannons for shredding starfighters, and a modular missile launcher capable of deploying both high-explosive and armor-piercing ordnance—allowing Panaka to adapt quickly to a wide range of combat scenarios.

Max speed: 5.0; Shield points: 5000; Hit points: 4000

Weapons: x2 AP/HE Missile Launcher, x4 Heavy Flak Laser Cannon, x5 Dual Light Turbolaser

Fleet commander:

Always stacks with other fleet commander bonuses.

SP: 4500 (50/s) HP: 3500 (12.5/s), Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 5, Agility: 0.7 Active Abilities: Sensor Jamming, Point Defense System (0.4s/750m) Passive Abilities: Galactic Stealth, Astromech Repair

Weapons: x4 Seeker Torpedo Launcher, x4 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x4 Dual Light Turbolaser

Obi-Wan Kenobi is perhaps the greatest embodiment of Jedi ideals the Order has produced in generations. He became everything his late Master hoped he would be: disciplined, wise, and unwavering. From a cautious Padawan at the dawn of the Separatist crisis, Kenobi rose to become a legendary warrior, a steady mentor to Anakin Skywalker, a respected voice on the Jedi Council, and a peerless general of the Grand Army of the Republic. But greatness bears a heavy cost. Should he falter in even one of these roles, the consequences for the Republic—and for Obi-Wan himself—could be catastrophic.

Kenobi commands his personalized Arquitens-class heavy corvette, Short Negotiations, as his flagship. Outfitted with a suite of combat enhancements, including a sensor scrambler, point-defense laser system, and seeker torpedoes, it excels at neutralizing enemy corvettes and can hold its own against larger warships. The vessel is a direct extension of Kenobi’s measured, precise combat doctrine, controlled, deliberate, and deadly when provoked.

Fleet commander: Obi-wan Kenobi’s Soresu mindset inspires smaller ships to prioritize defense and stronger static positions. All corvettes and frigates on the field with him do -10% Damage and have -5% Movement, but gain +25% shields and +20% health.

Always stacks with other fleet commander bonuses.

Originally fielded as a medical and support vessel during the Clone Wars, the Pelta-class Hospital Ship Configuration (HSC) prioritizes fleet sustainment over direct combat. Unlike the later combat-oriented refits adopted by the Rebel Alliance, this variant retains its medical facilities and repair suites, providing passive area-of-effect repairs to nearby friendly warships. Equipped with only a limited point-defense system and a modest hangar capable of supporting a single starfighter squadron, the Pelta HSC is best employed as a backline support craft, preserving fleet combat effectiveness while offering minimal protection against enemy strikecraft.

Required Planets: Ringo_Vinda, Rendili, Rothana, Allanteen, Corellia

Enhanced engines, reinforced hull plating, and upgraded shields improve survivability, while improved weaponry and targeting systems significantly increase its offensive capability. A strengthened point-defense system allows the Pelta ASC to effectively intercept incoming enemy ordnance, making it a reliable escort for larger, more vulnerable capital ships.

The Carrack-class light frigate is a compact, well-armed warship capable of engaging a wide range of targets. Equipped with anti-shield, anti-ship, and anti-starfighter weaponry, it poses a serious threat to corvettes, frigates, and strikecraft alike. However, its relatively weak reactor and shield generator limit its durability in prolonged engagements.

Designed for efficiency and ease of production, the Carrack serves well as an escort vessel and excels when deployed in wolfpack formations, where its versatile loadout and ion weaponry can overwhelm larger targets.

As the Clone Wars escalated and Separatist droid swarms began to overwhelm Republic fleets, the Navy commissioned a specialized Carrack-class variant to counter the growing threat. Sacrificing much of its anti-capital armament, the vessel was refitted with IRAS missiles, high-explosive warheads, and layered flak cannons, transforming it into a dedicated anti-starfighter platform. Colloquially known as the "Carrack Flak Frigate," it proved highly effective at shielding Republic capital ships from massed starfighter attacks.

Though largely ineffective against enemy warships, the Carrack Flak Frigate excels at escort duty, creating deadly kill zones with overlapping flak barrages and guided missiles capable of shredding entire squadrons before they reach their targets.

SP: 3500 (30/s), HP: 4500, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 3.5; Agility: 0.5 Sensor Range: 3000m, Max Engagement Range: 3500m Active Abilities: Power To Shields, Point Defense System (0.5s/1000m) Passive Abilities: None

Lieutenant Lorth Needa is a young and largely untested officer eager to prove himself in the Clone Wars. Hailing from a large and distinguished Coruscanti family, his privileged upbringing has afforded him few opportunities for real frontline combat. He now stands ready to deploy to the front, or to defend Coruscant should the war reach the Republic’s capital.

In training and combat simulations, Needa has already demonstrated a talent for aggressive wolfpack tactics, turning Separatist doctrine against itself through coordinated swarm assaults.

Needa commands the Integrity, a modified Carrack-class light frigate equipped for both offensive and defensive operations. Heavy flak laser cannons and a point-defense system provide exceptional protection against starfighters and enemy ordnance, while reinforced armor and an upgraded shield generator improve survivability in prolonged engagements.

Fleet commander: Fleet Commander: Captain Needa is a legendary practitioner of Wolfpack tactics, known in Imperial Doctrine as “Coordinated Attack Groups”. All Carrack-class frigates in battle with him gain +30% damage, +25% shield strength and +25% movement speed.

Originally designed by SoroSuub as a long-range cargo hauler, the Quasar Fire-class Bulk Cruiser was never intended for frontline combat. With the outbreak of the Galactic Civil War, however, these freighters were hastily converted for military service by the Rebel Alliance and other sympathetic factions desperate for transport capacity. Robust, reliable, inexpensive, and easy to modify, the Quasar is commonly repurposed as a mobile hangar and supply ship, capable of ferrying large numbers of starfighters, troops, and vital materiel across the galaxy. Respectable armor and a modest weapons suite provide basic protection, but weak shields and painfully slow speed leave the Quasar best employed well behind the front lines.

The Quasar Fire-class Carrier grants all friendly fighters, bombers, and gunships +5% hull strength, +5% shield strength, and +10% movement speed.

Required Planets: Sullust

Corellian Engineering Corporation Carcus Destroyer-273-class. A new cutting-edge design by CEC, the CD-273 is a highly advanced compact heavy frigate that hits hard but is only lightly armored. Configured for long-range fire support, electronic warfare, and anti-starfighter screening, its main weapon systems consist of two long-range precision concussion missile launchers and two long-range medium turbolasers. Secondary weapons consisting of heavy and medium laser cannons, as well as light and standard turbolasers, mean the CD-273 is able to take on just about anything frigate-sized or smaller. It also sports powerful engines, an active missile jamming system, and an electronic warfare suite that enables it to scramble enemy-targeting computers and drain their shield generator power. Very effective against corvettes and frigates. Vulnerable against heavily armored targets.

Max Speed: 4.35; Shield Points: 7850; Hit Points: 9400

Weapons: x1 Dual Light Turbolaser, x2 Turbolaser, x2 Medium Turbolaser, x2 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x2 Precision Concussion Missile Launcher, x6 Dual Medium Laser Cannon

This starship costs 100 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

Required Planets (Republic): Corellia
Special Structures (Rebel): R_Shipyard_2

SP: 10000 (100/s), HP: 10000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 2, Agility: 0.2 Sensor Range: 3000m, Max Engagement Range: 3000m Active Abilities: Deploy Master Repair Droids, Deploy Laser Defense Satellite Passive Abilities: Integrated Master Repair Droids, Fleet Logistics Support

Weapons: x2 Dual Turbolaser, x2 Quad Heavy Laser Cannon

Complement: 1 LAAT Gunship Squadron (1), 2 V-19 Squadron (2)

Originally developed by the Republic, the MTC (Modular TaskForce Cruiser) was engineered to provide a broad range of logistical and support capabilities through interchangeable mission modules. These modular systems allow the vessel to be rapidly reconfigured for roles including disaster relief, post-combat search and rescue, repair and salvage operations, planetary suppression and pacification, and deep-space exploration. The MTC is also capable of conducting extensive resource surveys, enabling the evaluation of newly charted systems for colonization and development. In combat, the MTC’s slow speed and poor maneuverability leave it virtually defenseless, restricting its deployment to rear-area support roles under the protection of a larger fleet.

Fleet Logistics and Repair Module: Reduces construction cost and build time by 15% (Corvettes), 10% (Frigates), and 5% (Capital Ships) on the planet this MTC is stationed over. Bonuses do not stack. In combat, Master Repair Droids repair friendly units in an area around the MTC and can be deployed to provide repairs at extended range.

Required Planets: Allanteen, Corellia, Fondor, Kuat, Ringo_Vinda, Rendili, Rothana

The Bothan Assault Frigate 4 (BAF-4), produced by Bothawui Shipyards, was envisioned as a versatile backbone warship that could be deployed in large numbers across the front. Outfitted with strong shields but relatively weak armor, the BAF-4 relied on staying power rather than brute endurance. Its varied and extensive armament—including ion cannons, heavy laser cannons, advanced proton torpedoes, concussion missile launchers, dual turbolasers, and heavy flak lasers—allowed it to effectively engage a wide array of targets.

A spacious internal hangar housed up to four squadrons of mixed strike craft, giving the frigate added flexibility in fleet actions. Though it lacked specialization in any one area, its balanced design made the BAF-4 a dependable jack-of-all-trades vessel, capable of adapting to whatever the battlefield demanded—so long as it wasn’t outmatched in raw firepower or durability.

Max speed: 4.35; Shield points: 12000; Hit points: 9500

Weapons: x2 Advanced Proton Torpedo Launcher, x2 Ion Cannon, x4 Quad Heavy Laser Cannon, x2 Heavy Flak Laser Cannon, x8 Concussion Missile, x8 Dual Turbolaser

Designed and produced by Rendilli StarDrive decades before the Clone Wars, the Neutron Star–class was an early Republic-era frigate intended to serve dual roles as both a warship and a bulk transport. Often referred to simply as a “bulk cruiser,” the class became a common sight along major trade routes and patrol sectors, its silhouette familiar enough to be casually dismissed by smugglers and spacers alike. By the time of the Clone Wars, however, the design was already showing its age, having been eclipsed by newer and more capable Rendilli warships such as the Dreadnaught-class Heavy Cruiser. As a result, the Neutron Star saw only limited frontline service and was largely relegated to secondary duties.

During the Galactic Civil War, the Neutron Star endured as a cheap and readily available alternative to modern capital ships, pressed into service by the Empire and local defense forces for patrol and anti-piracy operations. Armed with several triple turbolasers and numerous heavy laser cannons, it is capable of delivering steady, sustained fire, but its complete lack of ion weaponry or missile launchers leaves it poorly suited to engaging heavily shielded or armored opponents. Mediocre armor protection, merely adequate shields, and a small starfighter complement further underscore its limitations. Long obsolete as a true warship, the Neutron Star nonetheless lives on in widespread use among criminal syndicates and paramilitary forces, valued not for its strength, but for its availability, simplicity, and low cost.

Required Planets: Ringo_Vinda, Rendili, Rothana, Allanteen

The Gladiator-class Strike Carrier is a late Clone Wars–era design from Kuat Drive Yards, developed as a general-purpose carrier and heavy frigate. Equipped with large internal hangars for a substantial starfighter complement, the Gladiator combines fleet support capabilities with respectable frontline firepower. Though not intended for prolonged combat against heavier warships, its versatile arsenal of ion cannons, armor-piercing missiles, and turbolasers allows it to overwhelm corvettes and lighter frigates with ease. Compact, flexible, and heavily armed for its size, the Gladiator remained effective long after the Clone Wars and continued to serve throughout the reign of the Empire.

The Provocator-class Light Star Destroyer is a heavily modified variant of the Gladiator frame, refitted from its original support carrier role into a front-line combatant. Developed as a desperation weapon by Republic Loyalist forces, the Provocator trades hangar capacity, shields, and engine performance for greatly increased firepower and heavy armor, reinforced by a built-in missile jamming system.

Armed with a balanced array of ion cannons, turbolasers, and armor-piercing missiles, the Provocator is capable of engaging a wide range of threats. While it mounts several heavy laser cannons for limited anti-starfighter defense, it relies primarily on its jamming systems to disrupt incoming torpedoes. Durable and hard-hitting, the Provocator excels as a frontline tank, able to absorb punishment and hold the line so long as it is not overwhelmed.

SP: 10000 (75/s), HP: 15000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 2.5, Agility: 0.35 Sensor Range: 2450m, Max Engagement Range: 3450m Active Abilities: None Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment

Mass produced by Rothana Heavy Engineering for the Galactic Republic, the Acclamator-class Assault Ship was originally intended as a heavily armed troop transport capable of transporting entire armies between worlds. With the outbreak of the Clone Wars, it was thrust into frontline service against the Separatists. Its balanced armament of turbolasers, heavy laser cannons, and proton torpedoes proved effective early in the conflict, but the class was gradually outmatched by larger and more heavily armed warships. Nevertheless, thousands were produced, serving throughout the Clone Wars before continuing in Imperial service or finding their way into the hands of rebels, mercenaries, and criminal syndicates.

In combat, the Acclamator poses a serious threat to the enemy at close range thanks to its proton torpedo launchers. However, weak armor, fragile shields, and inadequate point-defense leave it with little staying power in prolonged engagements, and it can be picked apart by enemy bombers in a matter of seconds.

The Acclamator II-class Assault Ship was developed by Rothana Heavy Engineering as a cost-effective modernization of the original Acclamator. Improved armor, stronger shields, and an upgraded weapons suite including quad light turbolasers, quad heavy laser cannons, ion cannons, and advanced proton torpedo launchers greatly enhanced the vessel's combat effectiveness while preserving its role as a heavily armed troop transport. The result was a far more capable frontline heavy frigate without the expense of developing an entirely new class of warship.

SP: 10000 (25/s), HP: 10000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 2.5, Agility: 0.35 Sensor Range: 2000m, Max Engagement Range: 3250m Active Abilities: Medium Tractor Beam, Gravity Well Generator Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment

Weapons: x6 Dual Light Turbolaser, x8 Turbolaser

Complement: 1 V-Wing Squadron (2), 1 LAAT Gunship Squadron (2)

Built upon the proven hull of the widely produced Acclamator-class Assault Ship, the Warden-class Interdiction Frigate represented the Galactic Republic's first successful attempt to integrate gravity well technology into a frontline warship. Experimental gravity well projectors allowed the Warden to pull enemy vessels from hyperspace and prevent them from escaping into lightspeed, making it an invaluable support ship for trapping hostile fleets and securing strategic objectives.

The immense power demands of the gravity well generators overwhelmed the Acclamator's modest reactor, leaving little energy for the ship's weapons and defensive systems. As a result, its turbolasers fire at an abysmally slow rate, while its shield generator recoverS at a painfully sluggish pace. Possessing only enough firepower to deter small corvettes at best, the Warden is utterly unsuited for frontline combat and relies entirely on allied vessels to exploit the opportunities created by its interdiction systems.

Required Planets: Ringo_Vinda, Rendili, Rothana, Allanteen

The Dreadnaught-class, officially designated the Rendili Support Cruiser, is a modern refit of a venerable pre-war Republic cruiser. Armed with a variety of turbolasers, laser cannons, ion cannons, and missiles, the Dreadnaught serves as a well-balanced, general-purpose heavy frigate suited for frontline assaults, fire support, and escort duty. A respectable starfighter garrison and tractor beam projector further enhance its versatility, while thick armor plating allows it to absorb a surprising amount of punishment. Despite these strengths, its weak shield generator, broadside-focused main armament, slow speed, and poor maneuverability leave it at a disadvantage against more modern warships.

Required Planets: Ringo_Vinda, Rendili, Rothana, Allanteen

Introduced during the closing stages of the Clone Wars and carried forward into the early Imperial era, the Dreadnaught-class Mk. II represents a further refinement of Rendili’s venerable support cruiser design. This upgraded variant replaces the original forward armor-piercing missile launchers with heavy ion cannons, greatly enhancing its effectiveness against shielded warships, while the removal of the tractor beam projector makes room for a secondary shield generator capable of dramatically increasing shield regeneration. Retaining the thick armor and broadside-focused firepower of the original design, the Mk. II trades some offensive versatility for improved survivability and sustained combat performance, making it a resilient line ship well suited to fleet actions and prolonged engagements against capital-class opponents.

Required Planets: Ringo_Vinda, Rendili, Rothana, Allanteen

Captain Jan Dodonna is a rising star in the Republic military, earning widespread recognition after the decisive destruction of the Bulwark fleet at Anaxes. A disciplined and selfless officer, Dodonna is known for putting duty before ego, often placing himself in harm’s way to buy time for others—first at Anaxes, and later during the defense of Yavin Base as a Rebel. Beyond his battlefield record, Dodonna is also a key figure in the advancement of starfighter tactics and design, laying groundwork that would shape future doctrines across multiple eras.

Jan Dodonna commands the Ardent Hope, a Victory-class Star Destroyer equipped with enhanced emergency shield reserves and an expanded hangar bay, offering greater starfighter capacity than standard vessels of its class.

Max speed: 2.5; Shield points: 25000; Hit points: 25000

Weapons: x1 Heavy Ion Cannon, x1 Quad Turbolaser, x2 Dual Medium Turbolaser, x4 Heavy Armor-Piercing Missile Launcher, x6 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x7 Dual Heavy Turbolaser, x10 Medium Laser Cannon, x12 Dual Light Turbolaser, Heavy Concussion Missile System (24 missiles)

T1 Complement: 1 V-19 Squadron (4), 1 Z-95 CVB Squadron (4) T2 Complement: 1 Z-95 CVI Squadron (4), 1 ARC-170 Squadron (4) T3 Complement: 1 V-Wing Squadron (4), 1 BTL-B Y-Wing Squadron (4) T4 Complement: 1 Z-95 CVMR Squadron (4), 1 J-45 Sabre Squadron (4) T5 Complement: 1 R-32 Squadron (4), 1 J-45 Heavy Sabre Squadron (4)

Fleet commander: Captain Dodonna grants +15% shield strength and +10% engine power to all Republic starfighters.

Always stacks with other fleet commander bonuses.

Captain Terrinald Screed was a decorated officer of the Republic Judicial Forces who later rose to prominence within the Republic Navy. He favors a doctrine of decisive engagement, relying on breakthrough tactics delivered by a fast, maneuverable frigate and capital ship fleet. His strategic thinking was instrumental in the defeat of the Bulwark Fleet at Anaxes, in coordination with Captain Dodonna. Screed also enjoys a close rapport with Chancellor Palpatine, which has only strengthened his influence within the Navy.

Arlionne, a Victory-class Star Destroyer, serves as Captain Screed’s flagship within the Victory Fleet. Its custom loadout reflects the Captain’s personal preference for proton torpedo launchers over standard armor-piercing missile batteries, favoring heavier ordnance capable of breaking enemy lines with a single, decisive strike.

Max speed: 2.5; Shield points: 25000; Hit points: 25000

Weapons: x1 Heavy Ion Cannon, x1 Quad Turbolaser, x2 Dual Medium Turbolaser, x4 Heavy Proton Torpedo Launcher, x6 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x7 Dual Heavy Turbolaser, x10 Medium Laser Cannon, x12 Dual Light Turbolaser, Heavy Concussion Missile System (24 missiles)

Complement: 2 V-Wing Squadron (2), 1 LAAT Squadron (1)

Fleet commander: Captain Screed’s Decisive Battle doctrine improves the combat effectiveness of corvettes, frigates, and capital ships, increasing their shield strength by 10% and movement speed by 20%.

Always stacks with other fleet commander bonuses.

SP: 8500 (75/s); HP: 12000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 3.5, Agility: 0.45 Sensor Range: 2650m, Max Engagement Range: 3500m Active Abilities: Redirect Power To Weapons Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment

x1 Heavy LRAS Missile Launcher, x3 Medium Turbolaser, x4 High-Velocity Heavy Laser Cannon, x9 Medium Laser Cannon

Before the introduction of the famed Victory-class Star Destroyer, Kuat Drive Yards produced the Victory-II (V-2) “Longbow,” an early pre-war escort and support frigate designed to fill a niche role in the Republic Navy. Armed with three long-range medium turbolaser turrets, the Longbow provided accurate, sustained fire beyond the effective range of most opponents, supporting heavier warships and bomber formations from the rear. Its primary mission, however, was starfighter defense, achieved with several medium laser cannons, four high-velocity heavy laser cannons, and a bow-mounted heavy LRAS (Long-Range Anti-Starfighter) missile launcher that made frontal fighter attacks extremely costly.

Though effective against early CIS droid swarms, the Longbow’s limitations became apparent as more advanced and heavily shielded starfighters entered service. Poor armor protection, weak shielding, and a lack of dedicated ship-to-ship weaponry left the V-2 ill-suited for direct combat, and it was increasingly outclassed in fleet engagements. As naval doctrine evolved, the Longbow was rendered obsolete and gradually phased out in favor of newer, purpose-built anti-starfighter corvettes.

Commissioned by the Republic Navy and built by Kuat Drive Yards, the Victory I-class was developed as a heavy fire-support platform to complement the more versatile Venator. Its heavy turbolaser batteries, paired with armor-piercing missile launchers, gave it a clear advantage in frontline engagements, allowing it to punch through capital ship armor. Its heavy concussion missile system, meanwhile, proved devastating against droid starfighter swarms—threats the Venator struggled to counter effectively. After the rise of the Empire, the Victory I remained in active service, performing exceptionally well against the lightly equipped fleets of the early Rebellion. However, as the conflict escalated and the Rebels deployed more heavily shielded Mon Calamari cruisers and advanced strikecraft, the Victory I became increasingly outmatched and was gradually relegated to secondary theaters of war.

Max speed: 2.5; Shield points: 25000; Hit points: 25000

Initially developed as an upgrade to the Victory I-class, the Victory II ultimately evolved into a distinct platform with a specialized battlefield role. Where the Victory I excels at breaching armor with heavy turbolasers and high-yield warheads, the Victory II is engineered to counter heavily shielded vessels. Its powerful ion cannon arrays can rapidly drain enemy shields, while heavy mag-pulse missile launchers disable critical systems, leaving hostile ships vulnerable to allied attacks. Though it lacks the raw firepower to reliably engage heavily armored capital ships, it remains more than capable of overwhelming enemy frigates and lighter warships. The Victory II also retains its predecessor’s heavy and medium laser cannon batteries, providing a moderate level of anti-starfighter defense against bomber strikes. Quickly becoming a mainstay of the Imperial Navy, the Victory II serves as a valuable force multiplier—working in tandem with its older cousin to counter Rebel threats across the galaxy.

Max speed: 2.75; Shield points: 25000; Hit points: 30000

Weapons: x3 Dual Ion Cannon, x4 Heavy Mag-Pulse Missile Launcher, x5 Quad Medium Ion Cannon, x6 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x8 Quad Turbolaser, x10 Medium Laser Cannon, x12 Dual Light Turbolaser

T3 Complement: 1 V-Wing Squadron (2), 1 ARC-170 Squadron (2)

T4 Complement: 1 Z-95 R-32 Squadron (2), 1 BTL-B Y-Wing Squadron (2)

T5 Complement: 1 R-32 Squadron (2), 1 J-45 Squadron (2)

Required Planets: Kuat, Fondor, Kamino, Rendili, Ringo_Vinda, Rothana, Corellia, Allanteen, Coruscant

The Immobilizer-class Interdictor Frigate is a specialized support vessel built upon a modified Vindicator hull, adapted to accommodate powerful gravity well projectors and the enlarged reactor required to power them. These systems can forcibly pull ships from hyperspace and prevent enemy vessels from escaping into lightspeed. It also features a sophisticated long-range point-defense array that is highly effective against torpedoes, missiles, and other enemy ordnance.

The immense power requirements and internal volume occupied by the gravity well projectors leave little room for heavy armor or offensive weaponry. As a result, the Immobilizer suffers from weak shields, light armor, and only modest armament sufficient to defend itself against light warships. It is a support vessel first and foremost, relying on friendly escorts to protect it from direct engagement.

Required Planets: Kuat, Fondor

Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker possesses some of the greatest raw Force potential ever recorded. Once a slave, he rose rapidly through the Jedi Order, though his emotional attachments and defiance of doctrine have long concerned the Council. Publicly hailed as a fearless hero and champion of the Republic, cracks lie beneath the surface. Secretly married and prone to violent outbursts, Skywalker walks a dangerous path—one that may shape the fate of the galaxy.

Skywalker commands the Resolute, a modified Venator-class Star Destroyer featuring heavy ion cannons and a robust starfighter complement.

Fleet commander: Anakin throws himself into firefights with a near suicidal confidence that his men unfortunately share. All strikecraft, capitals, battlecruisers, and dreadnaughts rush in head-first, with 33% increased movement speed firing their weapons for 30% extra damage, at the cost of 30% shield strength.

Always stacks with other fleet commander bonuses.

Special Structures: Republic_Shipyard_3 Republic_Uplink_Command

Jedi Master Kazdan Paratus is tormented. He constantly hears the quiet echoes of all that he’s lost and the whispers of his perceived cowardice from Order 66. Paratus escaped the Temple to live in filth on the Industrial wasteland of Raxus Prime, utterly alone, for years. This pressure cooker of guilt and loneliness catapulted him into full blown madness, leaving him a raving hermit worshipping a replica of the Jedi Temple constructed out of trash when he was discovered. Kazdan has since eagerly applied his skills as a mechanic and salvager to the Republic Loyalist cause, even repairing a Venator hulk to working condition. However, his presence is not a positive one. The old master is incredibly insane and does not follow directives from the Republic Emergency Government. Worse, his constant conflicting orders to nearby clones create utter bedlam in the simplest fleet actions, necessitating a dedicated network of officers to mitigate him. In-game, Kazdan requires Fleet Officer support to balance out his debuffs and strong fleet support to crack shields before he is effective.

Master Paratus commands the Echoed Lament, a heavily modified Venator Star Destroyer. Notably, it features salvaged mass drivers and a complement of recovered droid starfighters.

Max speed: 3.25; Shield points: 16000; Hit points: 20000; 3 Vulture Droids (6), 2 Hyena Bombers (6), 2, Ugly Medium Squadrons (2)

SP: 15000 (125/s) HP: 30000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 2, Agility: 0.065 Sensor Range: 2750m, Max Engagement Range: 4500m Active Abilities: Heavy Tractor Beam Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment

The Invincible-class Heavy Cruiser is an aging warship dating back to the Old Republic, designed during an era when massive capital ships ruled the stars before advances in weapons and starfighter technology rendered many such vessels obsolete. Surprisingly cheap and easy to acquire in the modern age, these cruisers are best suited for anti-piracy operations and fleet fire support rather than frontline engagements.

Its primary armament, consisting of a heavy mass driver and a heavy turbolaser, are fixed forward, while multiple quad turbolasers and heavy laser cannons provide flank coverage. Secondary weapons include a complement of heavy armor-piercing missiles capable of devastating armored targets with ease. However, lacking ion weaponry, the Invincible-class struggles against heavily shielded opponents and is utterly defenseless against bomber attacks.

This starship costs 200 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

Manufactured by Kuat Drive Yards, the Venator-class Star Destroyer served as the Republic's primary capital ship throughout the Clone Wars, combining respectable firepower with an extensive starfighter complement. Constantly deployed across the galaxy, the Venator earned an impressive combat record and helped shape the design philosophy of future KDY warships. Capable of easily destroying most frigates, it can also hold its own against larger capital ships, though its limited ion weaponry leaves it at a disadvantage against heavily shielded opponents.

This starship costs 250 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

The Venator II-class Star Destroyer program was headed by then-Admiral Wullf Yularen during the late stages of the Clone Wars. Intended as a general overhaul of existing Venators, it resulted in a vastly improved warship at little expense. A more powerful shield generator was installed, and the main heavy turbolaser batteries were linked to an improved fire control computer, offering greater power output, accuracy, and range. Other improvements to the ship's firepower included the addition of heavy ion cannons and heavy plasma torpedoes, enabling the Venator II to shred enemy shields with ease. Anti-starfighter defenses were overlooked in favor of less accurate but stronger quad heavy laser cannons. Finally, the old SPHAT particle beam weapon was removed from the ventral hangar bay, allowing the Venator II to carry more starfighters into battle.

Ultimately, the Venator II program was short-lived, as it still suffered from the same unfortunate drawbacks as the original Venator, eventually being overlooked and finally cancelled in favor of the new massive Imperial-class Star Destroyers that were more in line with the controversial Tarkin Doctrine. Only a small number of Venator II's were produced.

This starship costs 250 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

Manufactured by Kuat Drive Yards, the Venator-class Star Destroyer served as the Republic's primary capital ship throughout the Clone Wars, combining respectable firepower with an extensive starfighter complement. Constantly deployed across the galaxy, the Venator earned an impressive combat record and helped shape the design philosophy of future KDY warships. Capable of easily destroying most frigates, it can also hold its own against larger capital ships, though its limited ion weaponry leaves it at a disadvantage against heavily shielded opponents.

This starship costs 250 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

A'Sharad Hett was the son and Padawan of the legendary Jedi exile Sharad Hett, who lived amongst the Tuskens until his death at the hands of Aurra Sing. Hett would go on to become a prominent Master in his own right who fought in numerous pivotal battles in the Clone Wars. However, the loss of his father, the Republic, the Jedi Order, and the respect of his people pushed him to the point of breaking. The Fallen Master set his eyes firmly on a private war of revenge, not just against the Emperor and Vader, but on every person that gave up on the old Order and left it to die.

Hett commands the modified Servator-class cruiser, Uli-ah Krayt (translates to: Child of the Krayt). The ship boasts extremely strong Super Heavy Proton torpedoes instead of the standard issue heavy plasma torpedoes.

Reserve max: 4x Arc-170_Squadron_Rep, 4x V-Wing_Squadron_Republic

Servator-class Star Destroyer. A product of desperation, the Servator-class is built utilizing the hulls of the Venator, being one of the few revanchist destroyers designed and constructed after the Clone Wars. Heavy bracing, structural reinforcement, and uprated generators to handle its numerous weapons all eat into the hangar capacity its predecessor once boasted, but it is a hard hitter as a result, capable of challenging Imperial destroyers in direct ship-to-ship combat. Heavy ion cannons and heavy plasma torpedoes give the Servator a devastating increase in anti-shield firepower. Armor increases, however, have not kept up—Servators have the pace but not the plating to withstand prolonged action.

Max speed: 3; Shield points: 30000; Hit points: 40000;

2 ARC-170 (4), 2 V-Wing (4)

Weapons: x2 Heavy Plasma Torpedo, x2 Medium Dual Turbolaser, x3 Light Turbolaser, x6 Medium Ion Cannon, x8 Heavy Laser Cannon, x8 Heavy Dual Turbolaser, x12 Heavy Dual Laser Cannon

This starship costs 250 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

Losing this ship will refund 7200 credits to prevent double garrison costs.

Required Planets (Republic): Kuat, Fondor, Kamino, Rendili, Rothana, Corellia, Allanteen, Coruscant, Ringo_Vinda
Special Structures (Republic): Republic_Shipyard_3

Madame Maarisa Zsinj is a veteran of the Stark Hyperspace War and the Clone Wars with a long, distinguished career as an admiral within the Judicial Forces and Republic Navy. Firmly disillusioned by the rise of the Galactic Empire and the increased sidelining of female Imperial officers, she defected after being ordered to take her beloved flagship to be decommissioned. Admiral Zsinj began efficiently targeting government ships and Imperial-aligned shipping, crippling early efforts to stabilize the Core and stalling the Reconquest of the Rim. She remains at large—a testament to both her skill as a guerrilla and the drop in command ability within the Imperial ranks after the fall of the Republic.

A specialized variant of the Venator-class, Retaliation is dedicated solely to naval supremacy. Its hangar bays have been reconfigured, removing all ground assault assets, including the SPHA-T weapon, in favor of expanded starfighter capacity and ship-to-ship enhancements. A reconfigured shield generator and tractor beam, protected by thick armor, render them impervious to proton torpedoes. Outfitted with dual heavy ion cannons and advanced targeting systems, Retaliation excels at crippling enemy warships. It serves as the personal flagship of Madame Maarisa Zsinj, de facto commander of the officially disbanded Republic Navy.

Madame Maarisa Zsinj is a veteran of the Stark Hyperspace War and the Clone Wars with a long, distinguished career as an admiral within the Judicial Forces and Republic Navy. Firmly disillusioned by the rise of the Galactic Empire and the increased sidelining of female Imperial officers, she defected after being ordered to take her beloved flagship to be decommissioned. Admiral Zsinj began efficiently targeting government ships and Imperial-aligned shipping, crippling early efforts to stabilize the Core and stalling the Reconquest of the Rim. She remains at large—a testament to both her skill as a guerrilla and the drop in command ability within the Imperial ranks after the fall of the Republic.

Upgraded with enhanced weaponry, armor, and shielding, Madame Maarisa Zsinj’s flagship, Retaliation II, leads the Republic Loyalists in their struggle to restore the Galactic Republic. This heavily fortified vessel boasts exceptional armor protection for a Venator, rivaling an Imperator-class Star Destroyer. Its firepower has been significantly improved, now featuring dual turbolasers, heavy flak lasers for increased anti-starfighter defense, and an advanced targeting system that allows engagements at greater distances.

SP: 30000 (250/s), HP: 60000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 3; Agility: 0.085 Sensor Range: 4250m, Max Engagement Range: 4750m Active Abilities: Assault, Deploy Fighter Repair Droids Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment, Point Defense System (0.75s/500m)

Complement: 5 V-Wing Squadron (20), 5 BTL-B Y-Wing Squadron (20) Hero Complement: Jaig Squadron, Red Squadron, White Squadron, Blue Squadron, Gold Squadron

A veteran of the Senate Guard and a respected captain during the Clone Wars, Sagoro Autem was forced into exile after the New Order began purging the Republic military. Refusing to accept the former Chancellor's illegal seizure of power, he returned to service when loyalist elements of the Republic military rose in rebellion. Now an Admiral, Autem commands the Star of Coruscant, a Secutor-class Star Destroyer whose greatest strength lies in the exceptional discipline of its veteran crew and the elite clone pilots of Jaig, Red, White, Blue, and Gold Squadrons.

Fleet commander: Admiral Sagoro specializes in armor-focused frontline combat, resulting in a +10% health and +10% damage boost at the cost of -25% shield strength for corvettes, frigates and capital ships.

Always stacks with other fleet commander bonuses.

This unit cannot be rebuilt if destroyed. Once committed, this vessel cannot retreat until the battle is over.

SP: 30000 (250/s), HP: 60000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 3; Agility: 0.085 Sensor Range: 3500m, Max Engagement Range: 4750m Active Abilities: Deploy Fighter Repair Droids Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment, Point Defense System (0.75s/500m)

Complement: 6 Eta-2 Squadron (36), 6 V-Wing Squadron (36), 2 ARC-170 Squadron (12), 2 BTL-B Y-Wing Squadron (12), 2 LAAT Gunship Squadron (12)

Developed by Kuat Drive Yards during the final years of the Clone Wars, the Secutor-class Battlecarrier was conceived as the Republic's answer to the Separatist Lucrehulk, functioning as a massive supercarrier capable of deploying thousands of starfighters and bombers. To maximize hangar capacity, much of its internal volume was devoted to hangar space and propulsion, leaving its reactor undersized for a vessel of its scale. Although armed with a respectable battery of heavy weapons, limited power generation results in slow firing cycles, sluggish shield regeneration, and only modest point-defense capability.

Lightly armored and poorly protected for its size, the Secutor was never intended to trade blows with enemy capital ships. Instead, it relies on its enormous starfighter complement and the protection of an escort fleet to overwhelm the enemy from a distance.

This starship costs 500 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

Required Planets: Ringo_Vinda, Rendili, Rothana, Allanteen

Designed and constructed by the Republic Emergency Government during the late stages of the Galactic Civil War, the Valiant-class Heavy Carrier was built to reassert space superiority through overwhelming force projection. Its extensive armament of heavy turbolasers, ion cannons, and heavy flak lasers provided formidable offensive and defensive coverage against all types of threats, while its massive starfighter complement, more than double that of the aging Venator-class, allowed it to dominate the battlespace through sheer fighter presence. Backed by heavy armor and powerful shield generators, the Valiant stood among the most lethal capital ships fielded in the Republic’s late-war arsenal.

This starship costs 250 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

Originally a civilian starliner, the Dauntless-class was repurposed into a heavy warship by the SoroSuub Corporation and is now one of the most formidable capital ships available on the black market. Armed with ten heavy quad turbolasers and ten heavy laser cannons, it excels in brutal broadside engagements, capable of holding its own against most military-grade warships with sustained fire. While equipped with redundant shield generators, their overall output is relatively weak—making the Dauntless highly susceptible to ion weaponry.

However, this vulnerability is balanced by its exceptionally thick, layered durasteel armor, which can absorb heavy punishment from turbolasers and missiles alike. A respectable fighter garrison and powerful defensive weaponry help deter smaller threats, but like most capital ships, the Dauntless is sluggish and an easy target for massed bomber wings. It should never operate without a capable escort.

Max speed: 2.0; Shield points: 20000; Hit points: 75000

Weapons: x10 Heavy Laser Cannon, x10 Quad Heavy Turbolaser

Required Planets: Sullust

Crowned at a young age, Queen Apailana was molded by the ideals of the Old Republic and quickly became one of its fiercest defenders. An Imperial assassination attempt shattered Naboo's diplomatic ideals, leaving Apailana a resolute leader, unflinching in her pursuit of justice and retribution against the New Order. Though still youthful, she commands with conviction, rallying her people and allies in defense of freedom and sovereignty.

Bravo Home is a unique Acclamator-class Assault Ship modified by the Royal Naboo Security Forces as Queen Apailana's personal flagship. Configured for fleet support, ion cannons and mag-pulse missiles allow it to continuously disable enemy warships while stripping away their shields. Master repair droids and a short-ranged point-defense system enable Bravo Home to repair and defend nearby allies. Its Naboo-designed shield generator produces nearly twice the output of a standard Acclamator and is protected by heavy armor, rendering it immune to enemy fire.

Jedi Haven: Queen Apailana provides safe haven to Jedi refugees at great personal risk. While orbiting a friendly planet, she may recruit up to FIVE (5) Jedi Refugee Squadrons at a time.

Queen Apailana proved to be a formidable monarch and a voracious defender of the Old Republic. The war between the New Order and the Republic resulted in the glorious liberation of Coruscant from the grasp of the Chancellor, in no small part due to Apailana’s contributions to the war effort. The Queen now works tirelessly with the reformed Republic Senate to reintegrate the former territories and to reform the structural failings that allowed the Empire to arise.

An Imperial Star Destroyer retrofitted by the Royal Naboo Security Forces, the Queen Amidala IV fields an advanced ion weapons array—an experimental loadout originally developed by the Imperial Department of Military Research and covertly acquired by Naboo engineers. Reinforced shielding and a robust complement of customized Naboo starfighters and bombers make it a powerful and symbolic presence in battle. Though unmistakably Imperial in silhouette, its heart lies with the people of Naboo. A plaque near the bridge bears a simple inscription: “Named for the pride of our world, to carry on her spirit.”

Max speed: 3; Shield points: 50000; Hit points: 80000

Weapons: x2 Repeating Light Laser Cannon, x2 Medium Ion Cannon, x6 Dual Turbolaser, x6 Ion Cannon, x8 Octuple Heavy Ion Cannon, x10 Dual Medium Laser Cannon, x20 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x28 Turbolaser

Complement: 1 N-1 Starfighter Squadron (3), 1 N-1B Starbomber Squadron (3), 1 PT-1 Gunship Squadron (2)

Before the ubiquitous Imperial-class dominated the galaxy, its predecessor, the Imperator-class served as the premier capital ship of the Galactic Republic in the final years of the Clone Wars, setting the standard for Kuat Drive Yards’ iconic dagger-shaped warships for decades to come. Featuring the same devastating broadside firepower as its successor, the Imperator was otherwise less capable in ship-to-ship combat. It lacked many of the heavier weapons and ion batteries that became standard on the Imperial-class, and was also less armored, with a notably underpowered shield generator for a vessel of its size.

Despite these shortcomings, the Imperator raised the bar for capital ship design and proved a formidable warship in its own right, more than a match for anything the CIS deployed—except the dreaded Allocator-class, which was purpose-built to counter it. Imperators continued to serve into the early days of the Empire before being retired in favor of the more advanced Imperial I-class.

Max speed: 3.25; Shield points: 30000 (175/s); Hit points: 60000

Weapons: x2 Repeating Light Laser Cannon, x2 Medium Ion Cannon, x6 Dual Turbolaser, x6 Ion Cannon, x8 Dual Heavy Turbolaser, x10 Dual Medium Laser Cannon, x20 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x20 Turbolaser

Building on the foundation of the Imperial I, the Imperial II was designed to for extreme ship-to-ship combat. While retaining the same overall hull design and structural integrity, the ISD-II boasts significantly improved shielding and a more powerful shield generator, greatly enhancing its endurance in prolonged engagements. Its main batteries have been upgraded to octuple turbolaser barbettes mounted to allow superfiring arcs, enabling it to concentrate all of its firepower directly forward—dramatically increasing its offensive output in head-on engagements.

The ISD-II also features a vastly expanded suite of ion weaponry, giving it the ability to quickly overload enemy shields. Its anti-starfighter suite has been overhauled with light turbolasers and heavy laser cannons better suited for engaging corvettes and gunships. To counter bomber strikes, the Imperial II is equipped with a long-range point defense system, offering limited but reliable protection. A focused brawler, the Imperial II excels when leading the charge in heavy fleet battles.

Max speed: 3; Shield points: 45000 (350/s); Hit points: 80000

Weapons: x2 Quad Heavy Ion Cannon, x4 Dual Heavy Ion Cannon, x8 Octuple Medium Turbolaser, x9 Dual Ion Cannon, x10 Ion Cannon, x12 Heavy Laser Cannon, x20 Light Turbolaser, x20 Dual Turbolaser

Required Planets: Coruscant, Kuat, Fondor
Special Structures: Republic_Shipyard_3

Fighter 20·Bomber 18·Gunship 16·Transport 14·Corvette 12·Frigate 10·Capital 10·SpaceStructure 10·Super 10

Built by Kuat Drive Yards in the final stages of the Clone Wars, the Tector-class was developed to counter the increasingly dangerous capital ships fielded by the CIS, such as the Allocator and Lucrehulk. Designed around raw durability and firepower, the Tector featured thicker armor plating and a more powerful shield generator than both the Imperator and its later Imperial-class successor. Its heavy armament included heavy turbolasers and armor-piercing missile launchers, making it a formidable threat in direct capital ship engagements.

Unlike other Star Destroyers of its lineage, the Tector lacked a ventral hangar bay and carried no starfighter complement, leaving it highly vulnerable to bomber attacks and dependent on escort support. Despite this limitation, it proved highly effective in fleet combat and would serve as the design foundation for later Heavy Star Destroyers like the Allegiance-class. Tector-class warships remained in Imperial service through the Galactic Civil War, participating in numerous major engagements.

Max Speed: 3; Shield Points: 40000, Hit Points: 85000

Weapons: x1 Dual Medium Ion Cannon, x2 Heavy Armor-Piercing Missile Launcher, x2 Medium Ion Cannon, x2 Dual Heavy Ion Cannon, x5 Triple Medium Turbolaser, x8 Heavy Turbolaser, x10 Ion Cannon, x10 Light Turbolaser, x20 Quad Heavy Laser Cannon, x28 Dual Turbolaser

This starship costs 800 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

SP: 200000 (1000/s) HP: 450000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 3.5, Agility: 0.025 Active Abilities: Full Salvo (Turbolasers) Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment

Weapons: x3 Dual Medium Laser Cannon, x3 Heavy Proton Torpedo Launcher, x4 Heavy Concussion Missile Launcher, x16 Quad Turbolaser, x38 Heavy Ion Cannon, x42 Heavy Laser Cannon, x66 Dual Turbolaser

Complement: 4 V-Wing Squadron (24), 4 ARC-170 Squadron (12), 2 LAAT Gunship Squadron (8)

A relic of the Galactic Republic's naval limitations, the Praetor-class Star Battlecruiser is a powerful defensive platform boasting impressive layered armor and powerful shield generators for even by modern standards. While not as conventionally powerful as modern vessels of its size, the Praetor is more than capable of holding the line. These ships were pressed into frontline combat as the Clone Wars raged on, facing off against the increasing threat of larger and more powerful separatist dreadnaughts such as the Subjugator.

Required Planets: Ringo_Vinda, Rendili, Rothana, Allanteen
Special Structures: Republic_Shipyard_3

Developed by Kuat Drive Yards during the Clone Wars, the Mandator II-class Star Dreadnought was the Republic Navy’s answer to overwhelming Separatist numbers. Built to decimate lighter Confederate warships, it combined remarkable speed for its size with immense armor, allowing it to run down fleeing opponents. Lightly shielded by dreadnought standards, it relies instead on sheer resilience and firepower. Extensive batteries of standard, medium, and heavy turbolasers, supported by heavy ion cannons, provided near-total firing coverage, while long-range proton torpedoes and concussion missiles made it highly effective in siege operations.

The Variable Geometry Self-Propelled Battle Droid Mk. I, better known as the Vulture Droid, is a small unmanned starfighter that relies on overwhelming numbers to defeat its enemies. Lightly armored and armed, it compensates with high speed, strong maneuverability, and a small target profile that makes it difficult to hit in a dogfight. Produced in untold millions by Baktoid Armor Workshop and Haor Chall Engineering, Vulture Droids were a mainstay of Trade Federation naval forces before becoming a core component of the Confederacy’s war machine. Degraded by neglect and corrosion, these models have reduced structural integrity.

Required Planets: Mustafar, Muunilinst, Cato_Neimoidia, Nimban, Pammant, Neimoidia, Foerost

SP: 60 (5/s), HP: 60, Armor: Heavy, Max Speed: 3.85, Agility: 1.575 Active Abilities: Hunt, Deploy Flares Passive Abilities: Cortosis Armor: 25% chance to negate incoming damage 5 units per squadron.

Medium Repeating Laser Cannon: 450 m range, rapid-fire, 12 DMG

One of the few manned starfighters in CIS service, the hardy Utapauan Porax-38 features high-capacity shields and thick cortosis-inlaid armor capable of limited blaster deflection, and is well known for its deadly hit-and-run performance. Its twin repeating TAU-9 medium laser cannons, while somewhat inaccurate and short-ranged, are capable of sustained fire, making the Porax-38 a lethal weapon against unsuspecting foes. While durable, the Porax presents a large target profile when maneuvering and suffers from generally poor handling. This leaves it vulnerable to missile-armed craft in dogfights, where it relies on countermeasure flares to survive. Despite these shortcomings, its durability, firepower, and customizability made it a favored craft among bounty hunters and pirates long after the Clone Wars.

Required Planets (Empire, Rebel, Republic, Underworld): Utapau
